execution: Planning only. No live commands, flashing or wiring changes.
invariants: Never mask NE/FE/ORE/PE or auto-clear an error to obtain a passing result.
Preserve BKIN, voltage protections, command timeout and latched fault behavior.
No PC USB or grounded analyzer on the energized mains-referenced assembly.
Physical modifications only while de-energized and safely discharged.
Change one factor per comparison; separate host, low-voltage and powered evidence.
Exact message totals unavailable when counters saturate; do not divide errors by sequence changes as though they were total packets.
metrics: UART NE, FE, ORE and PE occurrences with timestamp and command state
CRC/integrity errors, dropped frames, sequence errors and resets
RX queue high-water mark and overflow occurrences
Target maximum IRQ latency and main-loop duration
Maximum telemetry age, HTTP timeouts and Wi-Fi reconnects separately
Sensor I2C errors and supply/reset evidence
Target fault-to-output-disable latency: not inferred from HTTP polling
No ENABLE acceptance after a pending transport fault and no automatic restart

variants.name: Installed baseline
variants.change: None; retain 709/708 and preserve comparable logs.
variants.test: Use the same observation window and build identity for each comparison.

variants.name: Pending RX fault guard
variants.change: Service already pending RX faults before consuming queued commands and dispatching a frame.
variants.test: 2240 scheduled cases plus existing host regression; then target timing and low-voltage verification.
variants.limit: Not an electrical-noise fix or an exhaustive instruction-level interleaving proof.

variants.name: Versioned CRC16 protocol
variants.change: Replace XOR checksum through an explicit peer protocol upgrade.
variants.test: Single and paired bit flips, bursts, truncated/replayed frames and legacy-peer rejection.
variants.limit: Improves corruption detection, not RX electrical quality; both peers and diagnostics must change consistently.

variants.name: Circular DMA RX
variants.change: Compare current ISR/ring reception with circular DMA and bounded parser consumption.
variants.test: RX load, wrap boundaries, DMA errors, IRQ latency and no stale command replay.
variants.limit: DMA can reduce CPU servicing pressure but cannot repair an electrically corrupted bit; motor DMA resources must be audited.

variants.name: Nonblocking TX
variants.change: Compare blocking replies with interrupt or DMA transmission, using an owned persistent TX buffer.
variants.test: Reply ordering, buffer lifetime, busy/error handling and maximum loop duration.
variants.limit: Current TX is in the main loop with interrupts enabled. A benefit or a cause of NE is not established.

variants.name: Baud rate sweep
variants.change: Compare 115200, 57600 and 38400 on both peers, retaining the same protection deadlines initially.
variants.test: Message wire time, reply timeout, traffic utilization and observed error rate.
variants.limit: A 32-byte 8N1 reply takes about 2.78, 5.56 and 8.33 ms respectively. The current 5 ms TX timeout is incompatible with the two lower rates; evaluate timing offline before deployment.

variants.name: Diagnostic traffic load
variants.change: Compare reduced versus normal nonessential logging/polling; retain command heartbeat and fault recording.
variants.test: CPU load, maximum frame age and Wi-Fi loss versus UART errors measured separately.
variants.limit: Do not suppress fault evidence or stretch watchdog deadlines to hide failures.

variants.name: Bounded parser resynchronization
variants.change: Define an inter-byte deadline and deterministic header recovery after a damaged/partial frame.
variants.test: Every truncation point, header bytes inside payload, random prefixes and recovery without auto-rearming.
variants.limit: Improves recovery after corruption; not permission to resume drive after a latched error.

variants.name: Reset and timing diagnostics
variants.change: Expose reset reason, boot/session identity, queue high-water and target loop/IRQ timing through a reviewed diagnostic schema.
variants.test: Intentional low-voltage reset versus UART fault versus Wi-Fi interruption, preserving the first cause.
variants.limit: Better diagnosis, not a repair; do not infer brownout solely from counter rollback.

variants.name: Reference and supply integrity
variants.change: Qualified on-site verification of UART reference path and local supply integrity; compare a reviewed correction if a defect is found.
variants.test: Suitable isolated measurements correlated with UART and I2C faults.
variants.limit: Shared powerbank does not establish the quality of the signal return. Do not remove all UART reference paths.

variants.name: Signal cable geometry
variants.change: Compare a short controlled route with each signal accompanied by its reference return, rather than arbitrary long jumper leads.
variants.test: Document actual length/route and receiver waveform, keeping other variables fixed.
variants.limit: Distance from motor wires alone does not prove immunity; all rewiring is de-energized.

variants.name: Receiver edge conditioning
variants.change: Evaluate source damping or an appropriate receiver buffer/filter only after measuring edge distortion and input levels.
variants.test: Rise/fall time, threshold margin and timing across supply/baud limits.
variants.limit: No blind capacitor/resistor values; an RC filter can itself damage sampling margin.

variants.name: Differential or isolated UART transport
variants.change: Keep the UART command protocol but replace the single-ended physical link with a reviewed differential or isolated design.
variants.test: Full-duplex versus half-duplex requirements, reference/common-mode limits, isolated power domains, delay and fail-safe behavior.
variants.limit: Requires additional hardware. RS-485 alone is not galvanic isolation and cannot be assumed safe for a mains-referenced assembly.
